title: Tavern / shop specialty
_note: Phase 9.6 Tavern oracle: what the place is known for — a noun phrase read after the sign ("known for {specialty}"). Lowercase, no terminal punctuation (the composer handles it). All weight 1.

entries.value: a dark, bitter ale brewed down in the cellar
a fish stew the regulars swear by
cheap, watered wine and cheaper rooms
roast meat, loud singing, and louder arguments
a house spirit that could strip paint
honeyed mead and hard bargaining
black bread, hard cheese, and harder looks
game pies of uncertain contents
a mulled wine famous three towns over
eels, however you least want them
a back-room card game that never quite ends
music from a blind fiddler most nights
the only clean beds for a day's ride
smuggled spirits, if you know to ask
a stew pot that has never once been emptied
cider that kicks like a mule
fresh bread and stale gossip
roast fowl turned on a dog-driven spit
watered ale and an honest fire
a wine cellar longer than the menu
a dwarven stout thick as tar
spiced wine and worse company
the last decent coffee before the wilds
a bottomless soup and a well-locked strongbox
trencher bread and trickster's dice
smoked meats hung from every beam
strong tea for those who don't drink
a grog the sailors won't name
